description: Lock-in as form: open with the tonic's third in doubt, lift the whole track a step into a new minor key inside the quietest valley, then refuse to modulate again for nine minutes. Two different valleys (one quiet, one low), then a six-minute rising plateau that never comes back down, closing with the loudest peak in the track as the exit.
name: diagnostic_overload

sections.name: Intro
sections.notes: Sub-only opening (centroid ~309 Hz, rolloff ~402 Hz). Sparse, low. Vocals enter at 5.5 s. Let the spectrum fill in fast once the voice arrives.

sections.name: First statement
sections.notes: Eb minor with ambiguous third — both minor and major third present, key detector flipping at low confidence. Energy rises sharply around 0:35 (-21.4 to -16.0 dB) and holds.

sections.name: Valley I
sections.notes: The dynamic floor: -26.0 dB at 2:55. The whole-step lift to F minor happens inside this valley, almost unnoticed. Quiet emptiness.

sections.name: Rebuild
sections.notes: F minor consolidates; chroma top C/F/Ab. Steady climb back to -13 to -15 dB. The new key is now home — do not modulate again.

sections.name: Valley II (sub-hole)
sections.notes: Low emptiness, not quiet emptiness: centroid collapses to 281 Hz at 5:20, near-sub-only. The spectral bottom of the track.

sections.name: Long plateau
sections.notes: Six-minute rising shelf, mean -12.9 dB climbing toward -11 dB. No dips, no cliffs — tension is duration, not contrast. Do not break it up.

sections.name: Peak
sections.notes: Loudest sustained passage: mean -11.5 dB, RMS max -10.2 dB at 10:25. Hold near the maximum — the peak is a shelf, not a spike.

sections.name: Outro
sections.notes: Do not wind down. Loudest single peak (-0.9 dB) lands at 11:55, final window is the brightest/noisiest in the track, then a hard stop. Ends in F minor at full volume, mid-sentence.
